# `dump --stage checked` prints what makes a declaration foreign.
#
# It printed the declarations stripped of their marks: a native was an
# ordinary `func shout(s string) string`, a field SNGL cannot model was a bare
# `bad dyn` with the reason gone, and both read as declarations a backend
# would emit -- the opposite of what they are.
#
# The round trip is the assertion worth making, and it is a CLI script rather
# than a golden because it runs the compiler twice over its own output:
# dump, check what came back, dump that, and require the two dumps to agree.
# A rendering that loses a mark checks clean and differs on the second pass.

sngl dump --stage checked app.sngl
cp stdout first.sngl

# What came back is a program, not a transcript of one.
sngl check first.sngl

# And re-dumping it reaches the same text, so nothing was lost on the way.
sngl dump --stage checked first.sngl
cp stdout second.sngl
cmp first.sngl second.sngl

# Each mark survived, with its arguments.
grep '#\[go\.native\("example\.com/todo", "todo\.Todo"\)\]' first.sngl
grep '#\[go\.native\("ID"\)\]' first.sngl
grep '#\[go\.native\("example\.com/todo", "todo\.Fetch", fails, context\)\]' first.sngl
grep '#\[macro\.unusable\("functions returning multiple values are not supported"\)\]' first.sngl
grep '#\[go\.native\("example\.com/todo", "todo\.Count"\)\]' first.sngl

# A declaration the host already has is emitted by nobody, so it prints with
# no body. The checker synthesizes `return <zero>` for a bodyless func, and
# printing that back read as a real implementation returning zero -- which,
# beside the mark, is the shape the checker itself refuses.
! grep 'return Todo\{\}' first.sngl

-- app.sngl --
import go "sngl:language/go"
import macro "sngl:macro"
import . "sngl:ui"

#[go.native("example.com/todo", "todo.Todo")]
struct Todo {
    #[go.native("ID")]
    id int
}

#[go.native("example.com/todo", "todo.Fetch", context, fails)]
func Fetch(q string) Todo

#[go.native("example.com/todo", "todo.MultiReturn")]
#[macro.unusable("functions returning multiple values are not supported")]
func MultiReturn()

#[go.native("example.com/todo", "todo.Count")]
var Count int

window {
    text(value="{Count}")
}
